time._notes: Clock speed lives in living.day_seconds (real seconds per game day at 1x); 3x and 10x divide it.

appeal_saturation._notes: Phase 2b appeal-to-attendance saturation. Below threshold, appeal passes through unchanged (the early/good-run park at appeal ~1.3 is unaffected). Above threshold, a diminishing-returns curve caps effective appeal near cap: effective = threshold + (cap - threshold) x (raw - threshold) / (raw - threshold + k). At appeal 3.0 effective is ~1.55; at 5.0 it is ~1.57. The heavy compression breaks the appeal->attendance->revenue->more dinos->more appeal compounding loop that blew NW past $9M, and the reduced revenue constrains reinvestment (fewer dino purchases, fewer upgrades), creating a secondary feedback that further limits growth.

attendance._notes: M2.6: base_demand 60 -> 72 (+20%). Elasticity 0.35 -> 0.6 with a new price_penalty_exponent of 2 (M2.6 playtest-2 fix): at 0.35 a $20 ticket earned as much as a $5 one, so the overspend trap paid for itself. Overcharging is now penalised by the SQUARE of the overcharge, so ticket revenue peaks near $7-8 and collapses above it: a $20 ticket empties the park (0.5% of demand) instead of paying as well as $5 did. Satisfaction (restrooms, tour guides) softens the curve, so investing in visitors is what buys the right to charge more. The reference price is unaffected (priceFactor(reference) = 1), so the classic $5 opening is unchanged. empty_park_factor 0.25 -> 0.15: a park with no living dinosaurs pulls a trickle of visitors and cannot cover its own costs. Cleanliness decay per day = cleanliness_decay_per_day x clamp(attendance / cleanliness_decay_ref_attendance, min_factor, max_factor): an empty park barely gets dirty, a packed one needs more maintenance. M3 carry-over: empty_park_factor 0.15 -> 0. A park with no living dinosaurs has no appeal, so demand and attendance are 0 and concessions (which scale with attendance) earn nothing: an empty park cannot profit.

revenue._concession_notes: Concession saturation: effectiveFactor = concession_cap x rawFactor / (rawFactor + concession_k). At low tiers (factor 1.3) this is near-linear; at max tiers (factor 3.3) it caps well below the raw sum, so each upgrade tier adds less than the last. Phase 2b: k 1.7 -> 2.3 to compress the high-end concession revenue curve and keep reinvestor NW under $1.5M.

advertising._notes: M4: the fixed campaign list moved to data/campaigns.json (a ladder with unlock conditions). Shared marketing mechanics live in balance.marketing.

goals._notes: M5 end-game ladder (src/goals.js). Goals fire once, in any order, and are listed in the Goals panel with live progress. loan_repaid: debt at zero. net_worth: cash + assets - debt at or above target. species: that many distinct species alive at once. rating_quarter: a quarter closes with the park rating at or above stars. grand_park: every facility at its top tier AND every spend-threshold prize earned AND rating_quarter stars held for consecutive_quarters quarter closes in a row; fires once with the big fanfare and the Grand Park plaque at the gate. report_card: opens at the close of year `year` (day = year x 4 quarters x 90), grades A-F per metric from the thresholds below (score >= A -> A, >= B -> B ... else F), one comment per grade, overall = mean of grade points (A=4 .. F=0). Profit = summed profit over the final year; attendance = average visitors per day over the final year; welfare = average health of living dinosaurs minus welfare.death_penalty per death and welfare.escape_penalty per escape over the whole game (floor 0); education = Visitor Center tier x education.per_tier + min(education.fact_cap, Fact Book cards opened x education.per_fact) + education.school_bonus if the school program ever ran; satisfaction = mean over the final year's quarter closes of (rating / max stars) x 100. Everything else about a report card is copy.

living._notes: dino_label_always lists the sizes whose pens always carry a name chip; now the real sprites are readable it is empty, so pen name chips show only on hover (they were blocking the view of the animals). Set it to ["small","medium","large"] to bring back always-on labels. day_seconds is THE clock: one game day at 1x takes this many real seconds (M2.6: 6). 3x/10x run proportionally faster; agents cap at max_speed_factor. M3: day_seconds is the DEFAULT; the Settings view lets the player pick any value between day_seconds_min and day_seconds_max (state.settings.day_seconds) and the clock, visitor spawn rate and autosave all read the live value. Starving dinosaurs keep a slow breathing bob (dino_starving_bob_hz / _px) so they never read as frozen. tram_speed/tram_pause_seconds drive the Park Tram along the forecourt track (visual only). M5: truck_speed / truck_pause_seconds / crate_seconds / pop_seconds drive the delivery-truck arrival (real seconds, runs even while the clock is paused); arrival_max_wait_seconds skips the truck for a purchase the living view has not shown by then; puff_seconds is the dust puff on a prize placement and a dinosaur pop. pen_label_stack_gap_px: interlocking pens whose species-chip stacks would land within this many px of each other are pushed apart (sideways inside their own pen, else lifted). Phase 3: sprite_scale is a global multiplier on the pixel-art dino sprites (sprites/manifest.json holds each one's per-size pixel height: small 32 / medium 48 / large 64 at the 960x540 logical canvas); dino_sprite_scale still sizes the fallback drawn shapes used until an image loads.

parcel._notes: space_per_tile x parcel tile count = enclosure capacity in space units. area_factor scales biome plot_cost by tile count (sub-linear: big parcels are a modest per-tile discount); counts missing from the table use count ^ area_factor_exponent. Fence cost = per segment x outline edges (tile edges not shared inside the parcel).

events._notes: pause_at_speed_max: at game speeds above this, non-critical events go to the ticker and the daily digest instead of a modal. pause_kinds: event effect kinds that always open a modal (plus foreclosure, win milestones and the Quarterly Report, which are not events). 'starving' is the daily starving-dinosaur warning: an asset about to die pauses the clock even at 10x.

save._notes: Autosave every N days (default = one quarter). The Settings view lets the player pick between the min and max; state.settings.autosave_days overrides the default.

prizes._notes: Prize fanfare toast lifetime. Thresholds live in data/prizes.json.

facilities._notes: Cap on the summed appeal_bonus from facilities (visitor center, museum store) plus park prizes, added to the appeal multiplier. Phase 2: 0.6 -> 1.0 because restrooms and the vet clinic now carry appeal too and a full park would otherwise waste its top tiers.

biome._notes: M4 biome mechanic (species biomes in dinosaurs.json). A dinosaur in a PREFERRED biome has its popularity multiplied by preferred_popularity and regains preferred_regen extra health per day. TOLERATED is neutral. The WRONG biome multiplies popularity by wrong_popularity and drifts health down by wrong_health_drift per day, but never below wrong_health_floor: the animal is unhappy, worth less and easier to lose to illness, yet the biome alone never kills a paid-for asset. The ticker/digest warns about each unhappy pen every warn_every_days. Re-landscape (enclosure panel) costs relandscape_ratio x the new biome's parcel price and wipes the pen's vegetation.

vegetation._notes: M4 seeds -> vegetation. Plant seeds (enclosure panel) in a pen: every seed unit adds to enc.seeded until the pen is fully planted at seeds_per_tile x tiles. Each day the pen's vegetation grows by growth_per_day[biome] x tiles x (seeded / fully planted), capped at veg_per_tile x tiles (a 4-tile pen holds 100). Herbivores graze whole units of vegetation before touching park stock (1 vegetation = 1 plant unit), and the roots keep regrowing after grazing. Growth is per PLANTED TILE, so a 4-tile marsh pen makes about 0.96 free plant units a day (two starter herbivores eat 2/day: ~48% fewer plants bought), plains ~30%, desert ~16%. A fully planted pen also adds appeal_bonus_per_pen x (vegetation / cap) to park appeal (shared cap: facilities.appeal_bonus_cap). Seeds are an investment: paid once, saving every day after; plants are a recurring cost. M5: visible_floor is the smallest share of a pen's greenery that is drawn once the pen has any seeds in it, so a freshly planted or heavily grazed pen still reads as seeded rather than bare.

food._notes: M4 food without round trips. warn_days: a low-food ticker/digest warning when a food type has fewer days of stock left than this (before the starving popup). restock_fill_days: the General Store Food tab pre-fills the quantity box with this many days of the park's daily need. auto_restock_default: the per-food auto-restock rule as it starts (off): when total stock of a food drops below threshold_days of need, buy amount units automatically and charge it (ticker + digest line).

marketing._notes: M4 marketing ladder (campaign entries: data/campaigns.json). weekend_days: day-of-week indexes (state.day % 7) that count as the weekend for the school program's weekday floor. stack_max: how many stackable campaigns (social media) can boost at once; non-stackable ones use only the strongest active boost. memberships: the season pass is priced PER QUARTER by the player between pass_price_min and pass_price_max. Each day, paying visitors convert to members at convert_base x satisfaction factor (convert_satisfaction_floor at zero satisfaction, 1 at the satisfaction cap) x price factor (1 while the pass costs at most fair_price_tickets tickets, then (fair / price) ^ price_exponent). Members visit member_visit_rate times a day each: that is the attendance floor, and those visits pay no ticket (they do buy concessions). At quarter close members churn at churn_base_per_quarter plus churn_extra_per_star for every star the park rating sits below churn_low_rating, then the survivors pay the pass price (Reports: Memberships line). Members never exceed max_members_per_capacity x the daily visitor cap. Phase 2 sweep (g): convert_base 0.006 -> 0.018 and churn_base_per_quarter 0.12 -> 0.10 so the pass reaches 15-35% of revenue averaged over its first eight quarters on a good park (it was 7-9%, still ramping; the member cap of twice the daily capacity holds the steady state under a third); churn_extra_per_star 0.2 -> 0.25 so a one-star park sheds its members to under a tenth within three quarters (0.62 a quarter, was 0.52).

overhead._notes: Property tax per quarter = (base + rate_per_tile x total owned parcel tiles) x difficulty overhead_mult. Teaches fixed vs variable cost: holding land costs money whether or not it earns. Standard pays ~$700-$2500/q; Classic pays much more via a high overhead_mult. Phase 2b: 75 -> 115 to offset the secondary concession_spend revenue and cost reductions added to facilities; safe for Classic played-well (4/5 seeds survive at 2 tiles, mult 20).

juice._notes: M5 juice timings (src/ui/effects.js, src/sim/agents.js). floater_min_gap_ms: cash-delta floaters closer than this merge into one. shake_ms: escape screen shake. count_up_ms: Quarterly Report numbers count from 0 to their value over this long. tip_toast_seconds: first-quarter tutorial tips stay up this long (they show one at a time; the next waits for the current one to close). All of it collapses to instant/static under Reduce motion.
